draft.title: Erosion, transportation and deposition
card: Erosion
the wearing away of rock and soil by water, wind, waves and ice. It happens as moving agents scrape, hit and carry material off the land.
Transportation
the movement of eroded pieces from one place to another. Rivers, wind, waves and glaciers all carry material.
Deposition
the dropping of material when the agent slows down or loses energy. This builds landforms such as beaches and sand dunes.
Waves also carve coasts. They wear away the base of a cliff, and over time cliffs can retreat and leave stacks, such as the Twelve Apostles in Victoria.
draft.remember: Material is worn away, carried, then dropped. Each stage can make a different landform.

a.q: Wind blows sand off a dry flat and drops it in a pile that forms a dune. Which process built the dune?
a.why: The dune formed when the wind lost energy and dropped the sand. Transportation is the carrying of the sand, but the pile only formed when it was dropped, so that is deposition.
a.clue: Which process is about dropping material?

b.q: Waves hit a cliff at Port Campbell for thousands of years, and a rock pillar stands offshore where the cliff once was. Which process made the pillar?
opts: Erosion of the cliff by waves
Drops in sea level from cooling
b.why: Waves wore away the base of the cliff and the coast retreated, leaving the pillar behind. Deposition builds up material, so it does not carve a stack. A stack is left standing by what was removed around it.
b.clue: Was material taken away or added?

b.best: Erosion of the cliff by waves

problems.detail: 'Each stage can make a different landform' says more than the card. The card only shows erosion carving landforms (cliffs, stacks) and deposition building them (beaches, dunes). It never says transportation makes a landform.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer each. The remember line suggests every stage, transportation included, makes a landform, which the card does not teach.
